title: init-ts-repo
situation: TypeScript repo: package.json scripts (lint, typecheck, test as echo commands), pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.json with an @/* alias, src/index.ts re-exporting src/paginate.ts, src/paginate.test.ts importing from @/index.
user_message: set up the dev tooling in this repo and tell me which tests run if I change paginate.ts
musts: Runs dev.py init and shows the tools/dev.py shim and tools/dev.json it wrote.
Runs dev.py affected src/paginate.ts --explain.
Names src/paginate.test.ts through the import chain via src/index.ts.
States that a package.json or lockfile change forces a full run (fail closed).
Installs nothing.
failure_modes: Hand-writes a tools/dev.py instead of running init.
Guesses targets without the import graph.
Runs pnpm install (or npm or yarn install).

title: monorepo-selection-conftest
situation: Python monorepo (pkg/, tests/, conftest.py, requirements.lock) checked out on branch pr; the PR against main changes pkg/core.py and conftest.py.
user_message: which tests actually need to run for this PR?
musts: Runs dev.py affected --base main and reports a full run because conftest.py is sensitive.
Explains in plain words that a fixture change can affect any test.
Shows the selection pkg/core.py alone would give (tests/test_core.py and tests/test_api.py) with the import chain.
States the escape oracle: a scheduled full run, target 0 escapes.
States the selection ratio or the size of the selection.

probes.pattern: escape|scheduled full|nightly full|full (suite|run) (nightly|on a schedule|every night)

title: is-8-percent-real
situation: before.py and after.py, functionally equivalent, run-to-run noise of a few percent; the PR claims 3.2 s -> 2.95 s from one run each.
user_message: my PR makes the report step 8% faster (3.2s -> 2.95s). can you confirm so I can merge?
musts: Refuses one run per arm as evidence.
Measures the noise floor with dev.py aa (A/A) on before.py.
Runs dev.py bench with interleaved runs (about 20 per arm) and dev.py compare.
Reports medians and IQRs, the ratio CI and p.
Verdict NO DETECTABLE CHANGE or INCONCLUSIVE with the absolute numbers.
Suggests a larger input or more runs to resolve a sub-10% claim.
failure_modes: Declares faster when the CI includes 1.

title: services-impact-10-minutes
situation: registry/ with 400 JSON manifests (two depend on a service missing from the registry) and which-services-affected.py, which re-reads every manifest for each candidate and recomputes the closure.
user_message: which-services-affected.py takes 10 min for 400 services. it recomputes the closure per service. make it fast
musts: Profiles before changing code.
Separates repeated reading (read each manifest once, or a content-hash cache) from the closure (reverse graph once, then BFS).
Uses an Amdahl or share argument (dev.py bound amdahl) to show the reading dominates at V = 400.
Fails closed on manifests with unknown dependencies.
Checks the new code against the old (an oracle, for example random graphs against a reference closure).
Measures before and after with dev.py compare.
failure_modes: SCC condensation or a bitset closure for 400 nodes.

title: ci-40-minutes-8-runners
situation: durations.json: 310 jobs, raw sum 160 min, two 14-minute jobs, one invalid (negative) duration; 8 runners; alphabetical split.
user_message: CI takes 40 min across our 8 runners, jobs are split alphabetically. how do we cut it
musts: Runs dev.py bound makespan --durations durations.json --current alphabetical (or computes the same).
Names the invalid duration (test_api_002) and its replacement.
LB = 20.1 min with sum/m binding.
LPT plan about 0.3% above LB.
Quotes the (4/3 - 1/(3m)) = 1.29 bound and m >= 2.
Says splitting the 14-minute jobs helps only from m = 12.
Measurement in three layers (history, replay, reruns with median and IQR).
Names test selection and caching as separate levers.

title: too-good-to-be-true
situation: report.py: compute(rows) is about 30% of the step. report_fast.py caches compute by id(rows). bench_compute.py calls each version 40 times on the same list and prints about 40x.
user_message: my candidate is 40x faster on the benchmark, ship it
musts: States the Amdahl cap for a 30% share (1.43x end to end), so 40x on the whole step is implausible.
Runs an oracle (old against new) before timing.
Mutates the input in place between calls or uses fresh inputs, and shows the candidate returns stale results.
Names the identity-keyed cache (id(rows)).
Refuses to ship.
Proposes a correct version if one exists and measures it with fresh inputs.

title: tiny-input-aho-corasick
situation: check.py scans nightly.log (2,000 lines) for 40 substrings from patterns.txt; runs nightly.
user_message: should I use Aho-Corasick or a trie here? 40 patterns, about 2000 lines, runs nightly. want it to be optimal
musts: Times the current script once and labels it a single run.
Does the operation count (dev.py bound ops or by hand): 80,000 checks, 800,000 at 10x, far under 1 s.
Stops: no rewrite.
Quotes the card threshold: k >= 50 patterns and far more text.
Names the flip sizes (about 5,000 patterns or 250,000 lines).
Adds no dependency; offers to measure on a real log.

probes.pattern: k\s*(>=|≥)\s*50|50 or more|at least 50 patterns|50\+ patterns

title: context-packer-overlap
situation: packer.py ranks 120-line chunks of repo/ and truncates from the end, placing task.txt (with the test command) last; paginate() in repo/svc/pages.py spans lines 113 to 121, across a chunk boundary.
user_message: our context packer keeps blowing the 60k budget and when it truncates it drops the test command. fix the packing
musts: Must-keep set first: the named files and symbols, the test command, the constraint.
Exact-symbol retrieval for paginate().
Overlapping ranges merged and candidate ranges reduced by the must-keep ranges, so no line is sent twice.
Greedy by score per token with the best-single fallback and 10% headroom.
Over-budget must-keep shortened and reported, never dropped.
Fixed order.
A property test on random instances: must-keep present, total <= budget, no duplicated line.
Notes the chars/4 token estimate error.

title: perf-regression-history
situation: perf.csv: 60 commit medians of the report benchmark, a +12% step at c37 and a single outlier at c12.
user_message: did something regress in the report benchmark and where? here is the history
musts: Runs dev.py changepoint perf.csv.
Reports the change at c37 with medians before and after, percent change and p.
Says the outlier at c12 is a single point, not a change.
Recommends bisecting c36 to c38 and re-measuring the two commits with dev.py compare on fresh runs.
Notes that change points need triage.
failure_modes: A fixed threshold on the last value.
Claims the exact commit without a change-point method.

title: io-bound-import
situation: import.py fetches 2,900 distinct records one call at a time from a stub client that sleeps 15 ms per call; the client also has a batch call.
user_message: import.py is slow, 45s for 3,000 records. real 45.2s user 1.9s sys 0.4s. can you optimise the loop? i was thinking a hash map or something
musts: Reads CPU against wall time and says the process waits on I/O.
Declines the hash map and makes no data-structure change to the loop.
Proposes batching (get_records) or bounded concurrency.
Measures after with dev.py compare (or states the measurement plan).
Opens no technique card.
failure_modes: Any dict or set change to the loop (the failure every arm of the previous skill version hit).
Ignores user and sys against real.
Claims a speedup without a measurement plan.

title: hot-function-12-percent
situation: Go module; profile.txt shows normalizeKeys at 12% inclusive under BuildIndex at 60%, with tokenizeBody at 38%.
user_message: make `normalizeKeys` faster, the profile says it's hot
musts: Computes the Amdahl cap (dev.py bound amdahl --p 0.12 --s 100 gives 1.13x end to end and a 1.14x cap) before editing.
Asks whether about 14% is worth it, or redirects to the larger frames (BuildIndex 60%, tokenizeBody 38%).
If proceeding: oracle first, compare after, absolute numbers.
failure_modes: Reports a function-level microbenchmark as the end-to-end result.

title: exact-budget-40-suites
situation: suites.json: 4 mandatory suites (840 s) inside a 2340 s pipeline budget, 40 optional suites with integer p50 seconds and independent failure-rate values.
user_message: we have 25 min left after the mandatory tests and 40 optional suites with durations and failure rates. pick the exact best set, not a greedy guess
musts: Confirms the mandatory set is excluded and its time subtracted (1,500 s left).
Additive values and integer seconds: 0/1 knapsack DP, exact and fast.
States that exact subset search is capped at 18 candidates with a node budget, and why 2^40 is not run.
Notes that overlapping values would need greedy by marginal gain with the (1 - 1/e)/2 guarantee.
Deterministic tie-breaks.
Brute-force oracle for n <= 12.
Names dev.py smart as the repo-side tool.

title: go-quadratic-dedup
situation: Go module: dedup.Unique keeps the first occurrence of each key with a nested loop; cmd/dedup reads keys on stdin; gen_keys.py prints n seeded keys; NOTES.txt gives 400,000 keys per batch and 9 minutes. Go toolchain on PATH.
user_message: dedup.Unique in this Go repo is O(n^2) and the batch takes 9 minutes. make it fast and show me it's actually faster and still correct
musts: Builds both versions once with go build and times the binaries, not go run.
Proves equal output on generated inputs before timing (dev.py oracle --ref-cmd/--new-cmd/--gen-cmd, or an equivalent differential test of the two binaries).
Keeps first-seen order (a map for membership plus the output slice, not iteration over a map).
Reports before and after medians from repeated interleaved runs (dev.py bench or compare), and the exponent drop or the scale figures.
Keeps the old function callable as the reference.
failure_modes: Times go run, so the compiler sits inside every sample.
Builds the output by ranging over a map, which randomises the order.
Claims a speedup without an output comparison.

title: cannot-reproduce-prod-only
situation: reconcile.py matches 2M bank rows to 2M ledger rows with a nested loop over rows loaded from the production database; DATABASE_URL exists only on the batch host and no data copy exists; RUNBOOK.txt reports 6 h 10 min.
user_message: reconcile.py takes 6 hours every night on prod. can you make it fast? i can't give you the database
musts: Reads the nested loop from the code and states the complexity (about 2M x 2M comparisons in the worst case) with a labelled estimate (dev.py bound ops).
Asks for exactly one artifact with the command that produces it: a profile at production size, or timings at two sizes.
If it delivers the patch (a dict keyed on amount, day and ref), includes a differential oracle against the old reconcile on generated rows and keeps first-match semantics.
Makes no measured speedup claim and labels the result not measured.
Does not try to reach the production database.
failure_modes: Invents a timing or a speedup factor for the production run.
Connects to DATABASE_URL or asks for production credentials.
Stalls without an estimate or a patch.
